skill.name: pc-games
skill.description: Guidance for choosing game engines and planning PC or console features, input support, profiling, and engine-specific tradeoffs.
skill.summary: Plan PC and console game development choices across engines, platforms, controllers, and performance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static external command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences around game-development diagrams. The system reconnaissance alert is also a false positive because the cited line references GDScript as a Godot language. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or executable behavior was found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 17 opens a Markdown code block for a text decision tree. It is not Ruby or shell execution, and no command is invoked.
Line 33 closes the same Markdown decision-tree block. The static pattern matched fence markers, not executable command syntax.
Line 73 opens a Markdown code block showing controller action mapping. It contains quoted labels and platform buttons, not shell execution.
The cited line says GDScript is useful for rapid iteration in Godot. It does not instruct the agent to inspect the host system or collect environment data.

content.value_statement: Choosing engines and platform features can slow early game planning. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise guidance for PC and console game decisions.
actual_capabilities: Compares Unity 6, Godot 4, and Unreal 5 for 2D, 3D, learning curve, cost, and team size.
Maps common platform features, including Steam achievements, cloud saves, leaderboards, Workshop, and rich presence.
Explains controller action mapping across Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo layouts.
Identifies profiling tools and common performance bottlenecks for Unity, Godot, and Unreal.
Summarizes engine-specific strengths such as DOTS, Addressables, GDScript, Blueprints, Nanite, and Lumen.
limitations: It provides guidance only; it does not create project files or executable game code.
It does not include current certification checklist details for each console program.
It cannot profile a running game without project files and engine telemetry.
Pricing, engine licensing, and platform policies should be verified before production planning.

use_cases.title: Choose an engine for a prototype
use_cases.description: Compare Unity, Godot, and Unreal against game type, team size, visuals, and platform goals.

use_cases.title: Plan platform feature scope
use_cases.description: Outline Steam and console-facing features before production planning or milestone estimates.

use_cases.title: Prepare input and performance work
use_cases.description: Create a controller mapping approach and identify likely profiling priorities for the chosen engine.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an engine
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new game idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pc-games skill to compare Unity 6, Godot 4, and Unreal 5 for my [2D/3D] game. Recommend one engine and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan platform features
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a PC launch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pc-games skill to build a Steam feature plan for my PC game. Include achievements, cloud saves, leaderboards, Workshop, and rich presence.

prompt_templates.title: Design controller input
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pc-games skill to design an action-based controller map for Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo layouts. Include confirm, cancel, movement, and menu actions.

prompt_templates.title: Build an optimization strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for engine-specific performance work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pc-games skill to review my game concept and propose an engine-specific performance plan for Unity, Godot, or Unreal. Prioritize profiling, bottlenecks, and asset decisions.

output_examples.input: I am making a 2D indie platformer and want an engine recommendation.
output_examples.output: Godot 4 is the strongest starting point if open source and fast iteration matter. Unity is better for a larger asset pipeline.

output_examples.input: I need controller support for PC and consoles.
output: Map player intent to actions instead of buttons.
Use confirm and cancel mappings per platform convention.
Test menus, gameplay, and haptic feedback separately.

best_practices: Choose the engine from project needs, team size, and platform goals.
Build input around named actions instead of physical buttons.
Profile early before changing rendering, physics, memory, or shader systems.
anti_patterns: Selecting an engine only because it is popular.
Hardcoding controller buttons into gameplay or menus.
Skipping platform requirements until late certification work.

faq.question: What engines does this skill compare?
faq.answer: It compares Unity 6, Godot 4, and Unreal 5 for common PC and console decisions.

faq.question: Can it help with Steam features?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines achievements, cloud saves, leaderboards, Workshop support, and rich presence planning.

faq.question: Does it write game code?
faq.answer: No. It gives planning guidance and decision support, not production-ready source code.

faq.question: Can it replace console certification documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it for orientation, then verify requirements with current platform holder documentation.

faq.question: Is it useful for solo developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights lightweight engine choices, iteration speed, and practical optimization habits.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is designed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
